title: Peso Pluma Surprises Mexican-American Graduates at Historic Ceremony
summary: Imagine you're at your graduation ceremony, and suddenly one of the biggest music stars in the world walks on stage! That's exactly what happened at the City University of New York (CUNY) on May 2. They held their first-ever Mexican-American graduation ceremony, and guess who showed up? Peso Pluma! He was the special guest, and everyone went wild. Nearly 200 graduates from 14 CUNY schools were there, celebrating their hard work and Mexican-American heritage. One graduate, Rachelle Campos-Suarez, said, "I couldn't believe it when I saw him walk out!" The ceremony was organized by the CUNY Mexican Studies Institute to honor the students and their families. It was a historic moment that showed Mexican-American students belong in higher education. Peso Pluma's surprise appearance made it even more unforgettable. Way to go, graduates!
why_it_matters: When you see people who share your background succeeding and being celebrated, it can make you feel proud and motivated to achieve your own dreams, no matter what obstacles you face.

background_read: Peso Pluma (whose real name is Hassan Emilio Kabande Laija) is one of the biggest names in Latin music, known for hits like 'Ella Baila Sola'.
CUNY (the City University of New York) includes 25 colleges and serves over 275,000 students across New York City.
Many universities now hold special graduation celebrations for minority groups to honor their unique achievements and cultural heritage.
This was the first such ceremony for Mexican-American students at CUNY, making it an important milestone for the community.
